svg.text: BENCH WIRING — Arduino Nano ESP32 build
3.3 V logic throughout: the RC522 connects DIRECT — no level shifters, no AMS1117, no 5 V anywhere.
wire these next — the green button
is the ONLY thing that wakes the board
coil from the 6 V rail, diode BAND to +
Power the coil from a SEPARATE 6 V
source until the 1000 µF cap arrives —
a 1 A pulse can dip a shared rail enough
Add the two buttons and the buzzer.
The green button on D3 is the only thing that wakes the board — without it nothing happens.
Use 220 Ω LED resistors, not 470 Ω.
470 was sized for a 5 V board; on 3.3 V it gives ~2.5 mA and the LEDs look dim.
Boards Manager → Arduino ESP32 Boards → Arduino Nano ESP32. Library Manager → MFRC522.
First fob tapped becomes master. Second fob → 2 red blinks + long buzz. Hold red 5 s for admin.
